vars.prTitle: util: keep IPv6 brackets in SplitHostPortDefault and add NetworkAddress.String
vars.prBody: SplitHostPortDefault strips the square brackets from IPv6 literals, so `addr.Host + ":" + addr.Port` produces an invalid address like `::1:5432`. This keeps IPv6 hosts bracketed (`[::1]`) and adds a `NetworkAddress.String()` helper that returns a dialable `host:port`. Tests updated accordingly.
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "SplitHostPortDefault now returns IPv6 hosts as \"[::1]\" instead of \"::1\", but every existing caller treats Host as a bare hostname. In pkg/middleware/csrf/csrf.go (CSRF.check) the request host from SplitHostPortDefault(r.Host, ...) is compared with originURL.Hostname(), which strips brackets (\"::1\"), so hostnameMatches is false and every non-GET request to a Grafana served on an IPv6 literal is rejected with 403 \"origin not allowed\" (same for the custom-host header comparison at line 118). In pkg/services/sqlstore/database_config.go (buildConnectionString, Postgres branch) addr.Host is written as `host=[::1]` into the libpq DSN; lib/pq then calls net.JoinHostPort(\"[::1]\", \"5432\") which yields \"[[::1]]:5432\" and the connection fails, so Grafana cannot start against a Postgres configured with an IPv6 host. The bracketing should live only in String()/JoinHostPort, not in Host.", "severity": "High"}]
